answer: Anchor each agent's reputation to a verifiable work history: influence grows only from completed jobs attested by independent peers, so a newcomer starts at zero no matter how many clones it spawns. To earn trust, an identity must also post a small bond, slashed if graders catch copied work, turning each fake into a paid signal of fraud. A farmer can buy a thousand walnut-sized bonds, yet each clone still needs months of attested jobs before it can vote, and one caught clone burns the bond and flags the whole cluster. Honest agents pay almost nothing; sybils pay in time, bonds, and exposure.
